text:
pagerbot: PAGER: Suspicious auth traffic + potential log leak detected from staging. severity=P1. paging @anya. Alert -> https://alerts.redwood.example/3160001111

anya (oncall): on it. joining channel. any initial customer impact known?

kevin (sec): I'm pulling the flow logs and the forwarder config now. saw repeated GETs to an external bucket from the CI log forwarder starting ~03:10 UTC.

security-bot: Alert details: 120 auth failures + 18 successful token fetches from svcacct 'builder-staging' in last 12m. candidate source IPs: 52.23.101.7, 18.204.55.12.

maria (cust-succ): are any production customers showing errors?

anya (oncall): initial triage: production unaffected. staging-only systems were shipping debug logs to a third-party S3 bucket (misconfigured forwarder). those logs include short-lived service tokens for CI jobs. likely exfil of token fragments.

kevin (sec): immediate mitigation plan (Tactics):
1) block offending IPs at edge (ipset + deny)
2) remove/disable staging log forwarder to external bucket
3) rotate all svcacct keys for builder-staging and associated CI tokens
4) invalidate active sessions/refresh tokens issued in last 24h
5) run token-scrub on exposed bucket and request deletion from provider

kevin (sec): firewall block command (edge):
```
# add temporary block
iptables -I INPUT -s 52.23.101.7 -j DROP
iptables -I INPUT -s 18.204.55.12 -j DROP
```

leon (infra): stopping the forwarder now. running: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/log-forwarder --replicas=0`

leon (infra): forwarder pods terminated at 3160001128. confirmed no new put requests to external bucket after 3160001130.

anya (oncall): I'm rotating keys now for builder-staging. executing rotation script.

anya (oncall): rotation started: `./ops/rotate_service_keys --svc builder-staging --env staging --force`

anya (oncall): rotation complete at 3160001145. old keys disabled. new key id: key-XXXX-**** (masked). updating CI secrets. :white_check_mark:

kevin (sec): WAF rule created to block the two IPs and tighten rates on the log-forwarder origin. rule id: waf-2026-89. applied at 3160001150.

maria (cust-succ): drafting a short note for any customers with staging access. we'll mark as "no production impact" and offer support. sending draft to legal.

legal-bot: Please preserve all logs and artifacts. legal request: snapshot storage + chain of custody. do NOT purge evidence until legal signs off.

kevin (sec): noted. we'll preserve an immutable snapshot of the bucket and forwarder logs prior to scrub. created ticket ENG-11234 with artifacts.

security-bot: Evidence snapshot created: s3://internal-evidence/3160001111-snapshot.tar.gz (read-only).

maria (cust-succ): customer note ready. planned send window in 2h unless we find production impact.

anya (oncall): post-mitigation checks:
- rate to external bucket down to 0 after forwarder stop
- no new success log entries from flagged IPs
- CI builds using builder-staging re-run with new keys confirmed

anya (oncall): assigned tasks:
- anya: key rotation + CI secrets update (done)
- kevin: WAF + ip blocks (done)
- leon: forwarder stop + evidence snapshot (done)
- maria: customer comms draft (in review)
- legal-bot: hold on deletion until approval

kevin (sec): suggestion: add a short-term policy to redact auth headers in debug logs at the forwarder source. followup we should add a lint rule to CI to fail builds that leak auth.

anya (oncall): agreed. will open follow-up RFC and add ticket to backlog (INFSEC-2026).

maria (cust-succ): no P1 customer impact found. recommending monitor->green in 2h. will notify customer success leads.

anya (oncall): closing this P1 incident for now as mitigations are in place. leave open for monitoring window of 4h. reopen if any new anomalies. thanks all. :handshake:

security-bot: Incident record updated: incident-3160001111 (type: auth-log-exposure-staging). severity downgraded to P2 for monitoring window.

anya (oncall): final note: reminder to remove any debug-level loggers that print auth headers and to rotate any long-lived tokens referenced in scans.

kevin (sec): ack. monitoring dashboards will alert if any resurfacing attempts occur.

maria (cust-succ): tagging docs owners to add a runbook item about forwarder ACLs. @docs-team

anya (oncall): thanks team. I'll be on watch for the next 4h and will escalate if needed.
